titleOrRole: Professor of Physics, King Khalid University
bio: Prof. Dr. El Sayed Yousef is a Professor of Physics at King Khalid University, Saudi Arabia, and Director of AMIS Lab. His research focuses on the characterization and development of glass and glass ceramics for optical, photonic, sensing, and biomedical applications, spanning novel glass synthesis, crystallization behavior, and nano/microstructural characterization of bioactive glasses for bone tissue regeneration. He has led multiple funded research projects on tellurite-based glasses, rare-earth doped optical materials, and bioactive glass scaffolds, and has authored more than 300 papers in ISI-indexed journals.

titleOrRole: Professor of Physics, King Khalid University
bio: Prof. Dr. Alaa El Dein Ibrahim Dahshan is a Professor of Physics at King Khalid University, Saudi Arabia. His research focuses on amorphous semiconductors, chalcogenide glasses, and thin films, spanning their optical, electronic, photoelectrical, and thermal characterization — including composition-dependent refractive index behavior and crystallization kinetics studied via differential scanning calorimetry. He has led multiple funded research projects on chalcogenide thin films for solar cell absorption layers, thermoelectric and photovoltaic devices, and hydrogen production via water splitting, and has authored more than 300 papers in ISI-indexed journals.

Abdulaziz Ahmed Hadi Asiri is a PhD student in the Physics Department at King Khalid University, working on scientific instrumentation, optical systems, and terahertz spectroscopy. He built and validated a photoconductive-antenna-based terahertz time-domain spectrometer (THz-TDS) for materials characterization, and contributes to a collaborative project on light-phosphor sources for plant growth at the Central Laboratories Center. His published work includes a study on the terahertz optical and dielectric properties of BK7 silicate glass.

titleOrRole: Associate Professor, Department of Radiological Sciences, King Khalid University
bio: Dr. Khalid Ibrahim Hussein Ibrahim is an Associate Professor in the Department of Radiological Sciences at King Khalid University, where he serves as Bachelor Program Coordinator. He holds a PhD in Medical Physics from the University of Cape Town, South Africa, an MSc in Medical Physics from the University of Surrey, UK, and a BSc in Applied Physics and Instrumentation from the University of Gezira, Sudan. His research spans medical physics, radiation protection, radiotherapy, and nuclear medicine, alongside materials-science work on radiation-shielding glasses and functional oxide materials.
